s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic scalp lesions with disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages
salient_findings: Nonhealing crusted scalp lesions for 3 years
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages on the scalp
Yellowish crusts on the scalp
Osteolytic lesions on the right frontoparietal skull
Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei on biopsy
key_facts: 4-year-old boy
3-year history of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions
Previous treatments with topical glucocorticosteroids and antibiotics showed no improvement
Occasional otitis media
Negative family history for skin disease
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages on the scalp
Yellowish crusts on the scalp
Normal routine blood examinations
Osteolytic lesions on the right frontoparietal skull on whole-body MRI
Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei on punch biopsy of scalp
Infiltrate stained positively for CD1A on immunohistochemical staining
Normal ultrasonography of abdomen and lymph nodes
Normal serum electrophoresis

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic scalp lesions with disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages
salient_findings: Nonhealing crusted scalp lesions for 3 years
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages on the scalp
Yellowish crusts on the scalp
Osteolytic lesions on the right frontoparietal skull
Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei on biopsy
key_facts: 4-year-old boy
3-year history of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions
Previous treatments with topical glucocorticosteroids and antibiotics showed no improvement
Occasional otitis media
Negative family history for skin disease
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules and petechial hemorrhages on the scalp
Yellowish crusts on the scalp
Normal routine blood examinations
Osteolytic lesions on the right frontoparietal skull on whole-body MRI
Subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei on punch biopsy of scalp
Infiltrate stained positively for CD1A on immunohistochemical staining
Normal ultrasonography of abdomen and lymph nodes
Normal serum electrophoresis

differentials: disseminated cryptococcosis due to cryptococcus laurentii

raw.rationale: The presence of osteolytic lesions, subepidermal infiltrate with large cells and kidney-shaped nuclei, and positive CD1A staining on immunohistochemical staining, along with the clinical presentation of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions and petechial hemorrhages, are consistent with incontinentia pigmenti, a rare genetic disorder that affects the skin, hair, and other organs.

rejected.label: psoriasis
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic psoriatic plaques and scales, and no response to topical glucocorticosteroids

rejected.label: seborrheic dermatitis
rejected.why: Absence of typical seborrheic dermatitis distribution and morphology, and no improvement with topical treatments

rejected.label: plaque psoriasis
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and histopathological findings do not match those of plaque psoriasis

rejected.label: dermatitis
rejected.why: The specific findings of osteolytic lesions, kidney-shaped nuclei, and CD1A positivity are not typical of dermatitis
